messages.subject: Clarification of randef
parts:
Hi Dr. Chalmers,

I was looking into RIM models to understand the crossed effect of condition and gender on responses to each of my items my current model is:

items = colnames(data_longformat[4:25])
model = mixedmirt(data_longformat[4:25],1, random =~1|items:sex:condition, covdata = data_longformat[2:3], itemtype = “Rasch”)


In this model, sex and condition are factored binary variables. I extracted the random effects of the interaction of gender and condition on each item with randef along with the theta’s. I wanted to know that since I didn’t specify a fixed intercept does mixedmirt estimate the fixed mean intercept for all individuals and the random effects of my cross interaction are deviations from this fixed mean?

Thanks!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Clarification of randef
parts:
I believe the answer to your question is yes; mixedmirt() only automatically adds in a random effect for the person parameters. You have a random effect above pertaining to all combined levels of item*sex*condition, which likely has many unqiue random coefficeints. I'm not entirely sure what you're trying, but in such cases you usually want to satisfy the principle of marginality and also include the main random effect terms as well as the lower order interactions (not always required if there are nested effects, but this is generally the case). HTH.
 
Phil

messages.author: c2ee45de0a75c037
messages.subject: Re: Clarification of randef
parts:
Thank you as always for the clarification Dr. Chalmers. My intention was to model the interaction between Sex and each individual item at baseline and post-treatment. Consequently, I created a triple interaction term for the random effects believing that this was the syntax for the crossed design; however, I read the mirt package manual more closely and looked at the mixedmirt output and believe that my original syntax is incorrect. So, I believe that the correct syntax to state that the interaction of Sex:items is crossed with Condition (where each group interacts with the same item in pre and post condition) is random =~Condition:Item:Sex, where Condition is similar to a random slope. I had two intentions- 1) To obtain accurate person abilities that accounted for DIF based on sex, condition, and the interaction of sex and condition, and 2) Obtain the random item intercept deviations for each sex, convert them to item difficulties, and then obtain the probabilities of endorsement (for easier interpretations for my peers). Unfortunately, I believe that my original syntax may have treated that interaction has independent. Essentially, with my new syntax, I noticed that more random effects and covariances were modeled ( "COV_items:Sex_items:Sex", "COV_Condition_items:Sex", "COV_Condition_Condition") and this time, extracting the random effects with randef gives me a data frame with two columns, where I noticed that the first column was the baseline deviation from the fixed grand item effect for each sex, and the second column was the change in item intercept from baseline to post-treatment.

Thanks again!
